headline: UNIDIR examined fault lines since the NPT Review Conference and called for strengthening the Biological Weapons Convention, as Congress pressed its Nvidia national-security probe and the FCC approved SpaceX's plan for up to 1 million AI satellites.

points.text: UNIDIR took stock of the fault lines that persist six months after the 2026 Non-Proliferation Treaty Review Conference closed in New York.
UNIDIR argued for strengthening the Biological Weapons Convention to address the full biothreat spectrum, as the Working Group on Strengthening the BWC concludes its activities at the end of 2026.
Congressional committees are set to question Nvidia executives next week about AI chip exports and potential national security breaches.
Prominent Democrats demanded new restrictions on AI development after reports that OpenAI and Anthropic employees increasingly fear their most powerful models cannot be safely released.
Top AI executives are increasingly pushing back against a view inside Anthropic that humanity should surrender some decision-making power to superintelligent AI systems.
The FCC authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites into orbit as part of its 'Starmind' initiative.
The ITU's AI for Good discussed building shared global standards for foundation model evaluation.
